# IContentLoader&lt;TContent&gt;

[Framework](README.md) · `DotGame.Framework.Content` · interface

```csharp
public interface IContentLoader<TContent> : IContentLoader
```

Types: [`IContentLoader`](IContentLoader.md)

Loads a piece of content of type `TContent` from the configured content source.

## Remarks

Threading contract:

- [`LoadAsync`](#loadasync) MAY be invoked on the game thread or on a worker pool thread. Implementations must not assume either. While the game starts, `Content.LoadAsync` runs loaders on the game thread; after that it runs them on worker threads, except on the web, which has only the one thread.
- Decode/parse work runs inline on the calling thread. Implementations SHOULD NOT wrap their decode in `Task.Run`: `Content.LoadAsync` has already chosen the thread, and on single-threaded WASM it would only add continuations.
- Implementations MUST execute engine-restricted work on the game thread. This includes GPU resource creation and upload, shader compilation on platforms that require the device thread, and audio engine attach/connect. Use `GameThread.InvokeAsync(...)` — it short-circuits to a synchronous direct call when already on the game thread.
- `.ConfigureAwait(false)` SHOULD be used on awaited I/O calls so continuations don't bounce back to the game thread when the loader is running on a worker thread. It is harmless when the loader runs on the game thread (continuations stay inline).
- The returned `Task<TContent>` may complete on any thread. Callers that require the game thread observe it by awaiting from the game thread; the game synchronization context handles the hop.

See `docs/architecture/threading.md` for the full threading model.

## Methods

### LoadAsync

```csharp
new Task<TContent> LoadAsync(string contentKey)
```

Loads the content with a key, as its type.
